summary: The change maps cl_http_utility=>decode_base64 to a new abap.DecodeBase64. That function runs the existing Node-compatible DecodeXBase64 and passes the bytes to a new nodeutf8.Decode, a WHATWG-style UTF-8 decoder with one U+FFFD per maximal subpart. I compared nodeutf8.Decode with Node's Buffer.toString() on 200k random byte strings biased toward edge bytes and found 0 mismatches. I compared DecodeBase64 with Buffer.from(s,'base64').toString() on 100k random strings mixing both alphabets, padding and junk characters, also 0 mismatches. The new emit-go test passes, along with the full emit-go suite (15/15) and the listed acceptance and regression tests.

findings.claim: The end-to-end compile test skips without failing when .local/lars/open-abap-core is absent (for example on a fresh clone or a CI runner without the clone). Only the Go unit test in nodeutf8 then guards the NATIVE mapping. This follows the existing pattern but is worth knowing.
